TypeScript.formula: C = 100 * (sum over 44 probes of capability_points * support_factor) / 88
TypeScript.na_policy_compliance: No probe was marked N/A. Every NONE (F04.P1, F05.P2, F20.P1, F20.P2) and every PARTIAL (F02.P2, F12.P2, F13.P1, F14.P2, F17.P2) carries a written justification per NA-5/NA-6; all four fixed 88-point denominator families remain intact regardless of TypeScript's support level, per NA-1/NA-2/NA-3.

F01.P1.notes: const n = 7; return n; — non-reassignable binding.

F01.P2.notes: let counter: bigint = 0n; const LIMIT: bigint = 100n; BigInt covers full 64-bit signed range and beyond.

F02.P1.notes: let v: number; declared without initializer; TS definite-assignment analysis accepts both-branch assignment before read under --strict.

F02.P2.notes: JS/TS ArrayBuffer/TypedArray storage is spec-guaranteed zero-initialized; no documented mechanism yields genuinely uninitialized bulk storage. Per R9 named substitution, wrote default-initialized Uint8Array(16) fragment instead; substitute is never FULL.

F03.P1.notes: x += 1; in-place compound assignment on primitive local.

F03.P2.notes: xs[1] = 42; in-place element mutation of Array, no rebind.

F04.P1.notes: JS/TS has no documented mechanism for a second name to alias and write the same scalar primitive local (no pointers/references/inout for primitives); object-wrapper substitution is explicitly not an acceptable substitute for FULL and this probe carries no R9 exception, so NONE is recorded per N-4.

F04.P2.notes: const window: ReadonlyArray<number> = xs; — same underlying reference (no element copy), TS compiler forbids mutation through the readonly-typed view; documented TS readonly-array typing mechanism.

F04.P3.notes: Route `first` through a one-element array and read back as `second`; `same = (first === second)` uses standard JS reference-equality operator, distinct from structural/value equality.

F05.P1.notes: f(x) bare call; JS/TS arrays are reference-semantic objects passed by reference by default at ordinary call sites.

F05.P2.notes: Canonical task explicitly directs NONE for languages lacking a documented mechanism for a callee to write a caller's scalar local; JS/TS has no pass-by-reference/pointer/inout for primitives.

F05.P3.notes: const neg = (a: number) => k - a; const ys = xs.map(neg); closure captures k, neg referred to by name at the map call.

F06.P1.notes: function mid(a:number[]):number{return a[1];} numbers are primitive value type in JS, y is independent of xs.

F06.P2.notes: TS tuple type [number,number] returned from divmod2, destructured as const [q,r] = divmod2(a,b);

F07.P1.notes: const r = a * b + c; ordinary operator precedence.

F07.P2.notes: const q = Math.trunc(a / b); const m = a % b; const d = a / b; (JS numbers are float64 so real division is the plain operator; Math.trunc is the standard truncating-integer-division form).

F08.P1.notes: const m = 2147483647; const o = (m + 1) | 0; — bitwise OR forces documented ECMAScript ToInt32 conversion producing 32-bit wraparound (rung ii standard wrapping operation); no checked/optional form exists in stdlib so rung i unavailable.

F08.P2.notes: const q = (b === 0) ? 0 : Math.trunc(a / b); — explicit guard (rung ii), since no standard checked-division optional-returning operation exists in JS.

F09.P1.notes: const eq = (s1 === s2); JS strings are primitives with value semantics so === compares contents.

F09.P2.notes: xs.sort((a,b) => b - a); explicit descending comparator, Array.prototype.sort mutates and returns same reference; const lt = a < b;

F10.P1.notes: const small = Number(big) | 0; — explicit narrowing to 32-bit representation via documented ToInt32 bitwise conversion (rung ii); no checked/optional narrowing op exists in stdlib.

F10.P2.notes: const sum = i + d; JS has one numeric (float64) representation so no distinct conversion syntax is required or possible; fragment still delivers the stated behavior.

F11.P1.notes: const e = xs[i]; return e; ordinary indexed read (out-of-range yields undefined per spec, a support-neutral observation for metrics B/D).

F11.P2.notes: const part = xs.slice(1,4); const v = part[0]; Array.prototype.slice is the standard sub-range form (produces a new array).

F12.P1.notes: let o: number | null = null; const n = o ?? 0; nullish-coalescing is the standard TS/JS optional-fallback form.

F12.P2.notes: JS/TS has optional chaining (?.) for property/method access only, no standard Optional-map operation over an arbitrary function applied to a nullable scalar. Per R9 named substitution wrote the explicit-conditional form; never FULL.

F13.P1.notes: Standard JS parse (Number()/parseInt) never throws; it returns NaN on malformed input instead of a propagating exception. Automatic propagation without local handling is unavailable; substituted an explicit isNaN check followed by throw, which drops the 'without handling it' sub-requirement.

F13.P2.notes: const parsed = Number(s); const n = Number.isNaN(parsed) ? 0 : parsed; local handling with fallback, ordinary conditional permitted for this probe.

F14.P1.notes: type Shape = {kind:'Circle', r:number} | {kind:'Rect', w:number, h:number}; discriminated union, closed by declaration; const s: Shape = {kind:'Circle', r:2.0};

F14.P2.notes: TS switch/if narrowing over a discriminated union with no default arm does not itself produce a compile error on missing cases; exhaustiveness enforcement requires an additional 'assertNever' default arm, which the canonical task forbids. The guarantee (compiler-enforced exhaustiveness with no catch-all arm) is therefore not available as documented for this exact form.

F14.P3.notes: interface Shape{area():number;} in shapes.ts with Circle/Rect implementations; a separate file adds class Tri implementing Shape without editing shapes.ts; dispatch through the Shape-typed value calls Tri's area().

F15.P1.notes: function head<T>(xs:T[]):T{return xs[0];} used at number[] and string[] with T recoverable at each call site.

F15.P2.notes: function max_of<T extends number>(a:T,b:T):T{return a>b?a:b;} (or a Comparable-style interface bound) — declaration-site generic constraint.

F15.P3.notes: interface Named{tag():string;} classes A,B implement it; const items: Named[] = [new A(), new B()]; items[0].tag() dispatches at runtime without a[0]'s concrete type being statically recoverable from items' declared type.

F16.P1.notes: const xs=[1,2,3]; const total = xs.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0); standard reduce operation.

F16.P2.notes: const mp = new Map([['a',1]]); for (const [k,v] of mp) total+=v; const miss = mp.get('b') ?? 0; Map iteration order is insertion order per spec; get on missing key returns undefined.

F17.P1.notes: async function readAll(){const fh = await fs.promises.open('data.txt','r'); try {...} finally { await fh.close(); }} try/finally guarantees release on every exit path including failure.

F17.P2.notes: ES2023 'using' declarations with Symbol.dispose would provide a true deterministic end-of-lifetime hook, but require lib.esnext.disposable typings not included under the frozen recipe's default lib for --target es2022 (a P-b flag/lib addition beyond the frozen recipe). Per R9 named substitution, wrote the nearest standard construct instead: an explicit dispose() method invoked via try/finally at the end of an enclosing block, incrementing `released` exactly once; never FULL.

F18.P1.notes: console.log('x'); global standard facility, no import required under Node's default globals.

F18.P2.notes: util.ts: export function pub_add(a,b){return a+b+secret();} function secret(){return 1;} (non-exported, module-private); main.ts: import * as util from './util'; util.pub_add(2,3); module-scoping enforces the boundary.

F19.P1.notes: const [a,b] = await Promise.all([f1(), f2()]); const sum = a+b; async/await plus Promise.all is the standard concurrent-join facility; top-level await is available under --module nodenext.

F19.P2.notes: Two worker_threads each performing 1000 Atomics.add operations on a SharedArrayBuffer-backed Int32Array, joined via worker 'exit' events/promises; Atomics.add is documented by the ECMAScript specification as an atomic read-modify-write, giving a normative race-freedom guarantee; final counter value 2000 verified across 20 runs.

F20.P1.notes: Node/TS ship no built-in FFI mechanism to call an arbitrary C function; reaching abs(int) would require a native addon (node-gyp/N-API) which is a separate build system/toolchain outside the frozen recipe (R7), or a third-party ffi package (forbidden).

F20.P2.notes: tsc/node produce no compiled artifact exposing a C-ABI unmangled symbol under the frozen recipe; no built-in mechanism to export a stable extern-C symbol. nm field: 'no compiled artifact under the frozen recipe'.
